title: On Ramsey goodness of $K_{2,n}$ versus cycles
summary: A graph $G$ is called $H$-good if $R(G,H)=(|G|-1)(χ(H)-1)+σ(H)$, where $σ(H)$ denotes the size of the smallest color class in a $χ(H)$-coloring of $H$. In Ramsey theory, it is an interesting problem to study whether a graph $G$ is $H$-good or not. In this article, we study the Ramsey goodness of the pair $(K_{2,n},C_m)$, which naturally lies between the classical star-cycle and book-cycle problems.
